subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Helios Labs recommendation API throughput / pool sizing
messages:
From: Jason Rivera <jason@helioslabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T08:06:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial workload summary

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our internal ask, I'm sending a brief summary of Helios's recommender API workload so we can get an initial sense of committed GPU sizing and pricing. Attached is a CSV with 7 days of real traffic (Helios_Workload_Metrics.csv). High level: 

- Peak QPS (inference requests): 1,200 req/s (1% of minutes during business hours)
- Sustained QPS: ~300 req/s across 24h
- 95th percentile payload length: 3.2k tokens (context includes user history + product catalog snippet)
- Average response generation length: 150 tokens
- Typical concurrency per request path: many requests are independent; we see spiky bursts correlated with promotions
- Latency target: P95 generation latency <= 220ms (client side is sensitive)

We have an internal procurement window for May and are evaluating reserved commits (12-month) vs. shorter pilots. Can you outline: recommended GPU pool size (N GPUs of X family), expected throughput per GPU for this workload, and pricing tiers / discount guidance for a 12-month commit vs. 3-month pilot?

Appreciate any early guardrails.

—Jason
Head of Platform
Helios Labs

Attachments: Helios_Workload_Metrics.csv (CSV, 82KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Rivera <jason@helioslabs.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — initial workload summary

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Helios's workload. They want an initial recommended pool count, an explanation of how throughput maps to GPUs for their long-context recommender workload, and pricing tiers for 3mo pilot vs 12mo commit.

Key asks: sustained ~300 qps, peaks ~1.2k qps, 95th context ~3.2k tokens, P95 latency target 220ms. They mentioned promotion spikes and want predictable throughput and burst handling.

Can you put together a short modeling note with: 1) recommended GPU family (we've been recommending A100/80GB or equivalent for long context), 2) estimated sustained qps per GPU and recommended pool size with buffer for burst, 3) discrete pricing options (pilot vs annual commit) and discount bands (5/10/15% for commit tiers) plus any burst/overage rules.

Jason — we'll route the technical sizing through Ben and follow with a formal proposal.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

--
Attached: Helios_Workload_Metrics.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Rivera <jason@helioslabs.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — initial workload summary

Marissa, Jason — thanks for the data. I sketched a high-level throughput model below; happy to iterate if you share tail-latency targets for specific endpoints.

Summary recommendations (first pass):
- GPU family: 1 x L4-80 / A100-80GB equivalent per capacity block. For long contexts (~3.2k tokens) the memory footprint suggests 80GB-class; quantized weights can reduce memory but KV cache for long context still needs headroom.
- Throughput estimate (sustained): ~120–160 qps per GPU for the model size/latency target at 3.2k context (conservative assumption: single-stream generation with 150 output tokens).
- Peak handling: use a 1.8x buffer for burst traffic and autoscaling/burst pool to handle short spikes without degrading P95. So each GPU effective peak throughput ~200–280 qps for short bursts.
- Recommended committed pool: for sustained 300 qps -> 2–3 GPUs dedicated (300 / 140 ≈ 2.1) to meet steady-state. Add a burst reserve of 4 GPUs (shared autoscale) to reach 1.2k peak (with concurrency and request queueing). Operational configuration: 3 committed GPUs + 4 burst GPUs seems to balance unit cost and peak headroom.

Costing/packaging options (indicative):
- 3-month pilot: priced at list rate with 0% commit discount; includes basic support and 8-hour response SLA for infra incidents. Pilot pool: 2 dedicated + access to 3 burst GPUs.
- 12-month reserved commit: 3 committed GPUs with 20% discount (we can be flexible: 10% for 6mo, 20% for 12mo), priority capacity reservation, and inclusion of burst credits (20% of monthly token consumption convertible to on-demand capacity).
- Overages: any sustained overage beyond committed throughput billed at on-demand list price with a 10% overage credit if we fail to meet 95% availability SLA.

Questions for Helios (to refine):
1) What model are you planning to serve (open model name / size)? That changes per-GPU qps estimates.
2) How tolerant is the app to request queuing vs. cold-fallback to a smaller model?
3) Do you want predictable latency at peak (we can add a guaranteed throughput band) or is overall availability/cost the priority?

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with the per-GPU throughput curves and cost estimates after you confirm model target.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: per_gpu_throughput_estimate.xlsx (draft)

From: Jason Rivera <jason@helioslabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial workload summary

Ben / Marissa, thanks — this is a very helpful start. A few clarifications: 

- Model: we plan to serve an internally fine-tuned open decoder (7B–13B family) with 3.2k context using 4-bit quantization. We expect to switch to a larger 13B model for certain ranking endpoints later in Q3.
- Queuing tolerance: we can tolerate short tail queuing up to ~300ms for non-blocking experiences, but product recommends P95 end-to-end <= 300ms.
- Commitment appetite: procurement prefers 12-month commit but wants an optional 3-month ramp/pilot that will convert into the 12-month at signing. They asked if you can do a blended discount: 12-month price but 8% uplift for the first 3 months (transition pricing) — essentially a 12mo rate but slightly higher early months while traffic ramps.

Also: can you call out how many GPUs we'd need if we pre-emptively provision for the 13B switch (i.e., headroom path)? Appreciate the per-GPU spreadsheet when you have it.

—Jason

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jason Rivera <jason@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial workload summary (with 13B path)

Jason — with the model detail this adjusts numbers. Quick updates: 

1) Per-GPU throughput estimates (conservative, 95th-latency-aware):
   - For 7B family (4-bit quantized, 3.2k context): ~160–200 qps sustained per 80GB-class GPU
   - For 13B family (4-bit quantized, 3.2k context): ~70–95 qps sustained per 80GB-class GPU

2) Recommended commitment plan (to cover both phases):
   - Immediate pilot/ramp (months 0–3): 4 GPUs total (3 committed smaller units or 2 committed + 2 burst) to safely cover current sustained+buffer while we validate production behavior. Pilot billed at pilot rate with conversion option.
   - Full 12-month commit (post-ramp): 10 GPUs committed if you want headroom to run 13B permanently (targeting steady-state 300 qps on 13B would require ~4 GPUs (300/80≈3.75), but to safely meet 1.2k peak with minimal queuing and to support mixed-size models concurrently, we recommend 10 GPUs committed plus 4 in burst pool). This gives capacity to run horizontal replicas of both 7B/13B variants during A/B and can absorb promotion spikes with policy-based routing.

3) Pricing/discount suggestion: 
   - Pilot (3mo): list + standard pilot support; conversion clause: remaining 9 months of the 12mo commit billed at the committed rate if they sign before month 3 ends.
   - 12mo commit tiers: 8% discount for 5–9 GPUs, 18% discount for 10–19 GPUs, 25% discount for 20+ GPUs. For Helios (10 GPUs), recommend 18% off list with an introductory ramp premium for months 0–3 of +8% vs committed rate (Jason's ask) that sunsets on conversion.

4) SLA / throughput guarantees: We can offer a throughput SLO for committed capacity (e.g., guaranteed sustained qps per GPU with crediting for missed months). Burst pool remains best-effort but covered via burst credits included in the 12mo package.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with modeled qps curves for 7B vs 13B and a simple cost calculator across the commit tiers. Happy to jump on a call with procurement to walk numbers.

—Ben

Attachments: Helios_GPU_pool_model.xlsx, pricing_tiers_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jason Rivera <jason@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal summary & next steps — Helios Labs dedicated capacity

Jason — thanks for the quick responses and for the model detail. Below is a concise proposal and next steps we can present to procurement.

Proposal (concise):
- Pilot (months 0–3): 4 GPUs provisioned (2 committed + 2 burst). Pilot pricing: list rate; conversion triggers committed pricing for remainder of 12 months. Ramp premium: +8% during first 3 months if you choose the conversion clause.
- 12-month committed baseline (post-conversion): 10 GPUs committed (A100/L4-80 equivalent), with 4 burst GPUs. Rationale: supports migration to 13B family and provides capacity for promotions/A-B testing.
- Discount: 18% off list for 10-GPU committed band.
- Burst credits: 15% of monthly committed token units allocated to burst usage; overage billed at list with a 10% rebate if we miss a monthly throughput SLA.
- SLA & support: Priority support, 4-hour incident response for production-impact incidents, quarterly architecture reviews with Karthik/SE team.

Next steps: 
1) If this looks acceptable, we'll provide a formal SOW + pricing schedule and a HubSpot proposal link.
2) Procurement can review the ramp premium clause and confirm conversion timing.
3) Ben / Karthik to run a short cost-sensitivity spreadsheet with Helios's traffic mix (attached) and join procurement call next week.

I'll drop the HubSpot proposal link in follow-up. Thanks again — happy to take this to legal once procurement signals green.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
